description:
Send a two-finger circular arc gesture to rotate on-screen content by a specified angle. Two fingers are placed opposite each other at a fixed radius from the center, then swept from startAngle to endAngle degrees (endAngle > startAngle = clockwise). All positions and radii are normalized 0.0–1.0 (fractions of screen width/height, not pixels), same coordinate space as gesture-tap and gesture-swipe. Typical values: radius 0.15, startAngle 0, endAngle 90 for a 90° clockwise turn.
Size the orbit with radius, or with radiusX and radiusY together (the pair overrides radius); one half of the pair alone, or none of the three, is rejected. A single radius traces a physical ellipse on a non-square screen (finger separation varies through the turn); for a physically circular orbit, pass radiusX and radiusY with radiusX·width = radiusY·height.
Unlike gesture-pinch which moves fingers linearly to zoom, this orbits fingers in an arc to change orientation.
Use when you need to rotate a map, image picker, or any rotateable UI element. Returns { rotated: true, timestampMs }. On physical iOS, reactivated: true = app was re-fronted; re-describe. Fails if the simulator-server / emulator backend is not reachable for the given device, or on a physical iPhone when the app is not drawn in portrait.

radius.description: Distance from the center to each finger.

radiusX.description: Finger distance along the horizontal axis, as a fraction of screen WIDTH.

radiusY.description: Finger distance along the vertical axis, as a fraction of screen HEIGHT.

startAngle.description: Starting angle in degrees (0 = right, 90 = down)

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

name: gesture-rotate
